legal.reviewBanner: Legal review status: pending counsel review. This page restates factual product and security requirements from TaxDesk PK engineering specs. It is not a substitute for a firm-specific counsel-approved policy.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.metaDescription: How TaxDesk PK handles firm and client data, based on product security requirements.
privacy.intro1: TaxDesk PK is professional tax practice software for firms in Pakistan. This Privacy Policy describes how the product is designed to handle firm and client information according to current repository requirements.
privacy.intro2: Deploying firms remain controllers of their client data. Operators must configure retention, contacts, and any jurisdiction-specific notices for their practice.

scope.title: Scope
scope.body: This policy covers staff workspaces, the client portal, document processing, tax-year workflows, analytics, and administrative tooling shipped in TaxDesk PK.

tenancy.title: Firm and client isolation
tenancy.body: Access is designed around multi-tenant isolation:
tenancy.b1: Application queries are scoped by firm identifier.
tenancy.b2: PostgreSQL row-level security (RLS) isolates firm and client rows.
tenancy.b3: Portal users are scoped to their client; unauthorized cross-firm access is denied without revealing other tenants.

sensitive.title: Sensitive fields
sensitive.body: The product treats national identifiers and financial credentials as sensitive:
sensitive.b1: CNIC/NTN, full bank account numbers, IBAN, and stored IRIS credentials are designed for encryption at rest with per-firm envelope keys.
sensitive.b2: CNIC values are masked in the UI by default; revealing a full value is an audited action.
sensitive.b3: Account numbers default to last-four display; secrets are not shown again after entry.
sensitive.b4: AI extraction schemas require storing only CNIC last-four from AI output — never a fabricated full CNIC.

ai.title: AI processing and consent
ai.body: Document assistance may use external AI only under product guardrails:
ai.b1: Per-client AI consent is stored; per-client AI-off blocks external AI and falls back to manual or local flows.
ai.b2: Before external AI calls, CNIC, full account numbers, and postal addresses are masked in outbound payloads and re-attached locally after extraction.
ai.b3: AI call logs record metadata such as timestamp, firm, document, model, tokens, and cost — not raw document content.
ai.b4: Spreadsheet mapping sends headers plus a small sample of rows, not the full file.
ai.b5: Passwords for protected PDFs are used transiently in the browser and are not persisted.

retention.title: Retention and deletion
retention.body: Retention follows firm-configurable policy and owner-controlled deletion:
retention.b1: Files are retained per configured retention; temporary processing files are deleted after use.
retention.b2: Client archive retains data but removes the client from active lists.
retention.b3: Permanent client deletion requires Owner permission, typed confirmation, and an audit log entry.
retention.b4: Firm owners may request full export and deletion; deletion is logged and treated as irreversible in product requirements.

security.title: Security controls that protect privacy
security.body: Privacy depends on the security controls specified for TaxDesk PK:
security.b1: Staff authentication uses password plus mandatory TOTP; session tokens use HttpOnly Secure SameSite cookies, not browser localStorage.
security.b2: Uploads use magic-byte validation, malware scanning, size limits, encrypted object storage, and short-lived signed URLs.
security.b3: An append-only audit log records sensitive views, document access, AI calls, role changes, and related events.
security.b4: API surfaces require authentication on protected routes, input validation, rate limiting, and CSP headers.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: For privacy requests about a specific firm’s data, contact that firm’s Owner or administrator. Platform operators should publish a support contact for their deployment. Counsel review is required before treating this page as a binding legal policy.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.metaDescription: Terms for using TaxDesk PK, based on product responsibilities and tax-safety requirements.
terms.intro1: These Terms describe how TaxDesk PK is intended to be used. They restate product responsibilities from engineering and tax-safety requirements. They are pending legal review and may be replaced by firm- or operator-specific terms.
terms.intro2: By accessing a TaxDesk PK deployment you agree to use the software only for lawful tax practice operations and to keep credentials and client data confidential.

acceptance.title: Acceptance
acceptance.body: Use of staff, portal, or administrative features constitutes acceptance of these product terms for that deployment until superseding counsel-approved terms are published.

service.title: The service
service.body: TaxDesk PK provides firm workspaces for client CRM, document hub, tax-year files, computation, wealth reconciliation, return preparation, exports, billing, portal collaboration, analytics, and administration.
service.b1: Features depend on firm configuration, role permissions, and enabled integrations.
service.b2: Draft or placeholder tax rule packs keep computation and approval fail-closed until published rules are approved.
service.b3: Availability, backups, and recovery objectives are operational responsibilities of the deploying operator.

taxSafety.title: Tax calculations and professional responsibility
taxSafety.body: TaxDesk PK is a practice tool. It does not replace a qualified tax professional or official FBR guidance.
taxSafety.b1: Computed figures are estimates that require qualified review before reliance or filing.
taxSafety.b2: The tax engine is deterministic and versioned; large language models must not produce final tax figures.
taxSafety.b3: AI extraction produces draft data until staff confirm; humans approve return preparation and filing actions.
taxSafety.b4: The consulting firm and responsible professionals remain legally accountable for compliance and advice delivered to clients.

accounts.title: Accounts and access
accounts.body: Firms control user invitations, roles, sessions, and portal access.
accounts.b1: Staff must protect passwords and TOTP devices; sessions may be revoked by administrators.
accounts.b2: Portal OTP flows must not be used to probe whether a contact is registered outside legitimate client access.
accounts.b3: Sharing credentials or bypassing firm authorization controls is prohibited.

acceptableUse.title: Acceptable use
acceptableUse.body: You may not misuse the platform to harm clients, other firms, or system integrity.
acceptableUse.b1: Do not attempt cross-firm access, disable security controls, or exfiltrate data outside authorized workflows.
acceptableUse.b2: Do not upload malware or use document processing to evade lawful scanning and validation.
acceptableUse.b3: Do not use planning or computation features to facilitate tax evasion; product guardrails exist to discourage evasion patterns.

liability.title: Limitation of reliance
liability.body: Until counsel publishes deployment-specific liability terms, users acknowledge that TaxDesk PK outputs are decision-support only. Filing decisions, statutory interpretations, and client advice remain the responsibility of the firm and its licensed professionals.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: Product requirements may evolve. Material changes to published Terms should be versioned and communicated by the operator. This page will remain marked pending legal review until counsel signs off.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: Questions about these Terms for a given deployment should go to the firm Owner or the platform operator. Formal legal notices require counsel-approved contact details for that deployment.
